cues.feel: Shins pressing the boot fronts; weight even across the whole foot; quads relaxed, not burning.
cues.see: Hands visible in peripheral vision; skis running flat and quiet.

cues.feel: Smooth sliding; balanced over the middle of the foot; no urge to lean back.
cues.hear: Quiet, even hiss under both skis.
cues.see: Skis running straight; snow flowing evenly under both skis.

cues.feel: Gentle resistance building; speed bleeding off smoothly, not grabbing.
cues.hear: Soft scraping, even left/right. Loud scraping = too much edge, too much braking.
cues.see: Light spray from both inside edges, even side to side; symmetric wedge.

cues.feel: The turn "finishes itself" as the skis come across the hill; speed melts away without extra effort.
cues.hear: Scraping fades as the turn completes across the hill.
cues.see: J-shaped track; skis pointing across the hill at the end.

cues.feel: Rhythm — one turn flowing into the next; no panic between turns.
cues.hear: Consistent sound through each turn, no sudden loud braking.
cues.see: Round S-shaped tracks. Z-shaped tracks = turns not being finished.

cues.hear: Loud, uneven scraping from the tails.
cues.see: (student) tips of skis visible and light; snow blasting past. (instructor) hips behind ankles; spray from tails, none from tips.

cues.feel: Carved turns produce less friction → less vibration through the skis.
cues.see: Clean lines ("railroad tracks") vs skidded turns that leave scraped/sprayed snow.
cues.topic: Carving (Level 6 — reference example, out of V1 scope)

note: Layer 2 feedback: feel / see / hear — how the student knows they're doing it right. Not every entry needs all three.
